whatItIs: The feast of Christ's baptism in the Jordan River, and one of the most visible celebrations of the year.
whyItMatters: It remembers Christ being baptised by John the Baptist. Celebrating it each year is a way of remembering and renewing one's own baptism.
whatPeopleDo: On the eve, called Ketera, the tabots are carried in procession to a body of water
Priests bless the water and sprinkle the crowd
The tabots return to their churches the next day with singing and dancing
